title: Backspin, part by part
note: Written by hand from the code of the toy on the range page. Each step adds one part: a widget, items, or the loop.

steps.say: Make a paddle game. A canvas is the court: dark, 300 by 176 pixels, with a dashed net.
The court is a canvas. The proc px makes one rectangle of the palette, and a loop of px makes the net.
steps.check:
update
expr {[winfo class .c] eq "Canvas" && [llength [.c find all]] > 10}
steps.name: canvas: the court

steps.say: Use a scale as my paddle, on the left side of the court.
A vertical scale is the paddle. Its -variable pos is the top of the paddle, from 0 to the height of the court less the paddle.
steps.check:
update
expr {[winfo class .s] eq "Scale" && [.s cget -orient] eq "vertical" && $pos == 72}
steps.name: scale: the paddle

steps.say: Draw the two paddles, the ball, and the score.
Each paddle and the ball is a canvas item with a tag: me, cpu, and ball. The proc box moves an item to a grid of 4 pixels, for the pixel look.
steps.check:
update
expr {[llength [.c find withtag ball]] == 1 && [lindex [.c coords me] 1] == 72}
steps.name: canvas items: me, cpu, ball, score

steps.say: Make it move. The rival follows the ball, and a fast move of my scale gives the ball spin.
The proc tick is the game loop: after 16 ms it runs again. It reads pos, so the speed of the scale is the spin of the ball.
steps.name: after 16 tick: the game loop

steps.say: A click serves, and the arrow keys move the scale. First to 7 wins.
A click on the court and Space call serve. The scale has the focus, so Up and Down move it as its own keys do. The pad of the handheld calls toy_press.
steps.name: bind and focus: the keys of the scale
